title: Smart Home & IoT Privacy Security Checklist
metaDescription: Secure your smart home devices with our comprehensive IoT privacy checklist. Protect against tracking, hacking, and data breaches step-by-step.
intro: Your smart home devices are constantly collecting data about your daily habits, conversations, and routines. This checklist helps you secure your IoT devices, configure privacy settings, and protect your family from surveillance and cyber threats.

items.why: Voice assistants store recordings of everything they hear, creating a detailed record of your private conversations and activities.
items.howTo: Go to Alexa Privacy Settings or Google Activity Controls. Delete existing recordings and set auto-deletion to 3 months or disable saving entirely.

items.why: Prevents accidental or unauthorized purchases through voice commands, protecting both your wallet and children from making unintended orders.
items.howTo: In Alexa app: Settings > Account Settings > Voice Purchasing > Turn off. For Google: Assistant Settings > Payments > Turn off personal results.

items.task: Turn off drop-in and calling features
items.why: These features can be exploited by hackers to eavesdrop on your home or used inappropriately by family members.
items.howTo: Alexa app: Communicate tab > Drop In > My Household > Turn off. Google Home app: Assistant Settings > Voice Match > Turn off personal results.

items.why: Prevents your voice data and smart home usage patterns from being used to create targeted advertising profiles.
items.howTo: Alexa: Privacy Settings > Manage Your Alexa Data > Use of Voice Recordings > Don't use for ads. Google: Ad Settings > Ad Personalization > Turn off.

items.why: Physical mute buttons provide immediate control over when devices can listen, essential for private conversations.
items.howTo: Use physical mute buttons before sensitive conversations. Consider smart plugs for complete power control when maximum privacy is needed.

items.why: Third-party skills can access your voice data and smart home information, expanding your privacy risk beyond the main platform.
items.howTo: Alexa app: More > Skills & Games > Your Skills. Google: Assistant Settings > Services. Remove unused skills and review permissions for remaining ones.

items.why: Isolates smart home devices from computers and phones, limiting damage if IoT devices are compromised by hackers.
items.howTo: Set up guest network on router dedicated to IoT devices. Use different SSID name like 'Home-IoT' with WPA3 encryption if available, WPA2 minimum.

items.why: Default passwords are publicly known and make your entire network vulnerable to takeover by cybercriminals.
items.howTo: Access router admin panel (usually 192.168.1.1). Change both WiFi password and admin login. Use unique 15+ character passwords with numbers and symbols.

items.why: Router firmware updates patch security vulnerabilities that hackers actively exploit to gain network access.
items.howTo: Check router admin panel for firmware updates. Enable automatic updates if available. For older routers, check manufacturer website monthly for updates.

items.why: WPS has known security flaws, and remote management creates backdoors that hackers can exploit from anywhere.
items.howTo: In router settings, find WPS section and disable. Turn off remote management, cloud management, and any external access features unless absolutely necessary.

items.why: Provides additional protection against malicious traffic and alerts you to potential hacking attempts on your network.
items.howTo: Enable router firewall in security settings. Turn on DoS protection and intrusion detection if available. Consider upgrading to security-focused router.

items.why: Prevents unauthorized access to your camera feeds even if passwords are compromised, protecting against voyeurism and stalking.
items.howTo: In camera app settings, find Security or Account section. Enable 2FA using authenticator app rather than SMS for better security.

items.why: Video stored in cloud can be accessed by employees, shared with law enforcement, or breached by hackers.
items.howTo: Check camera app for cloud storage options. Consider local storage only or end-to-end encrypted cloud services. Review data retention periods.

items.why: Reduces unnecessary recordings of neighbors' property and public areas, respecting privacy and reducing false alerts.
items.howTo: Use camera app to set motion zones only covering your property. Exclude sidewalks, neighbor windows, and street areas from detection zones.

items.why: Audio surveillance may violate local privacy laws and captures private conversations of family, guests, and neighbors.
items.howTo: In camera settings, find audio options and disable recording. Keep video-only recording unless audio is legally required for security purposes.

items.why: Prevents recording when family is home, balancing security needs with personal privacy expectations.
items.howTo: Create recording schedules in camera app. Disable recording during family time, or use geofencing to auto-disable when residents are home.

items.why: Prevents unauthorized viewing of your home footage by family members, service providers, or hackers who gain account access.
items.howTo: Check camera app for shared users and permissions. Remove unnecessary access and limit sharing to specific cameras rather than full account access.

items.why: Many people lose track of IoT devices, leaving forgotten devices vulnerable and potentially spying on daily activities.
items.howTo: Check router admin panel for connected devices. List all smart TVs, thermostats, speakers, cameras, and other IoT devices. Document make, model, and purpose.

items.why: IoT devices are frequent hacking targets, and updates patch critical vulnerabilities that criminals actively exploit.
items.howTo: Check each device app for auto-update settings. Enable automatic security updates but review major firmware changes manually for privacy setting resets.

items.why: Default passwords are published online and used in automated attacks that scan for vulnerable devices to create hacking botnets.
items.howTo: Access each device settings through app or web interface. Change admin passwords to unique values. Use password manager to track device credentials.

items.why: Extra features like microphones, cameras, and location tracking increase privacy risks without providing security benefits.
items.howTo: Review each device app for features list. Disable microphones on devices that don't need voice control, location tracking, and usage analytics sharing.

items.why: Many devices share usage data with manufacturers, advertisers, and third parties for profiling and marketing purposes.
items.howTo: In device privacy settings, disable analytics sharing, usage statistics, and third-party data sharing. Opt out of marketing programs and research studies.

pro_tips: Use a privacy-focused browser when accessing smart home device web interfaces to prevent tracking cookies and maintain privacy during configuration.
Place smart speakers and displays away from bedrooms and private conversation areas to limit sensitive audio capture.
Consider local-processing devices like Apple HomeKit or Hubitat that don't require cloud connectivity for basic functions.
Regularly audit your router's connected device list to spot unauthorized devices that may indicate security breaches.
Create a 'smart home emergency plan' with steps to quickly disconnect all devices if you suspect a breach or privacy violation.
